brief: Goldman's economics team reports August PPI at +0.4% month over month (+5.4% year over year), in line with consensus, with energy prices rebounding 4.2% after June and July declines on the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran. Core PPI rose 0.2%, below the +0.3% Goldman and median forecasts, while PPI ex food, energy and trade services rose 0.3%, in line. The softer core reading does not carry into PCE: the PPI components that feed PCE were on net stronger than Goldman expected, driven by domestic passenger airfares (+4.2%, seasonally adjusted by Goldman) and medical care, from which the team estimates PCE medical care services rose 0.28%. Goldman therefore marks its August core PCE estimate to 0.24% from 0.22% before the release, a +3.15% year-over-year rate once its forecast of the revisions from the upcoming methodological changes is included. Existing home sales fell 2.0% to 3.98mn annualized, in line, with declines in every region except the West and months' supply up to 4.4 months. Initial claims fell 1k to 206k and continuing claims fell 1k to 1,774k, both in line. Goldman left Q3 GDP tracking unchanged at +2.5% annualized.
